members.name: flag
members.summary: True when a --flag (or its short form) is present in argv.

members.name: value
members.summary: The value of a --name option as an Option.

members.name: fromBase64
members.summary: Decode standard base64 (padded or unpadded) to Bytes. Raises on malformed input. Use it for binary data; Str.fromBase64 decodes to text.

members.name: fromHex
members.summary: Decode hex (upper or lower case) to Bytes. Raises on odd-length or non-hex input. Handy for crypto values such as fingerprints, moduli and EC points, which are usually written in hex.

members.name: hmacSha256
members.summary: Compute an HMAC-SHA256 of a message with a key (key first), returned as Bytes. To use a Secret as the key, pass `Secret.reveal s |> Str.toUtf8`; revealing a Secret is always explicit.

members.name: length
members.summary: The byte count as a Size.

members.name: sha256
members.summary: The SHA-256 digest of the bytes, as lowercase hex (same output as sha256sum).

members.name: sub
members.summary: A slice of the bytes by start index and length. Works like Str.sub, including the error when the range is out of bounds.

members.name: toBase64
members.summary: Base64 of the bytes, on one line. Use it to turn bytes into text, since print, JSON and YAML do not accept raw bytes.

members.name: toHex
members.summary: The bytes as lowercase hex on one line (the same format sha256 uses).

members.name: tryFromBase64
members.summary: Like fromBase64, but returns an Option: None for malformed base64.

members.name: blue
members.summary: Color the text blue. No color when output is piped or NO_COLOR is set.

members.name: bold
members.summary: Make the text bold; combine with a color by nesting. No styling when output is piped or NO_COLOR is set.

members.name: cyan
members.summary: Color the text cyan. No color when output is piped or NO_COLOR is set.

members.name: dim
members.summary: Make the text dim. No styling when output is piped or NO_COLOR is set.

members.name: gray
members.summary: Color the text gray (bright black). No color when output is piped or NO_COLOR is set.

members.name: green
members.summary: Color the text green. No color when output is piped or NO_COLOR is set.

members.name: magenta
members.summary: Color the text magenta. No color when output is piped or NO_COLOR is set.

members.name: red
members.summary: Color the text red. No color when output is piped or NO_COLOR is set.

members.name: sgr
members.summary: Style the text with a raw terminal escape code, for 256-color (`38;5;208`) or truecolor (`38;2;r;g;b`). No styling when output is piped or NO_COLOR is set.

members.name: underline
members.summary: Underline the text. No styling when output is piped or NO_COLOR is set.

members.name: yellow
members.summary: Color the text yellow. No color when output is piped or NO_COLOR is set.

members.name: copy
members.summary: Copy a directory and everything in it from src to dst. Raises if the destination exists; use Dir.deleteAll first to replace it. The copy is always recursive.
members.example:
let d = Path.newTempDir ()
Dir.copy d $"{d}-c"
Dir.deleteAll d
Dir.deleteAll $"{d}-c"

members.name: create
members.summary: Create a directory and any missing parents (like mkdir -p). Does nothing if it already exists, unlike copy and move, which raise on an existing destination.

members.name: delete
members.summary: Delete an empty directory. Raises when it does not exist, or when it is not empty (the error points you to Dir.deleteAll).

members.name: deleteAll
members.summary: Delete the directory and everything in it, recursively. There is no undo.

members.name: exists
members.summary: True when the directory exists.

members.name: list
members.summary: The full paths of the directory's entries, both files and directories, sorted by name and read immediately. Filter with Seq.where and File.exists/Dir.exists; for a recursive listing use `Path.glob "**"`.

members.name: move
members.summary: Move (rename) a directory from src to dst. Raises if the destination exists.

members.name: stat
members.summary: The directory's entries as FileRow values, the same rows ls shows, but for any directory (ls only lists the current one). Sorted by name and read immediately.

members.name: average
members.summary: The mean duration, truncated to whole milliseconds. Raises on an empty sequence.

members.name: h
members.summary: A duration of n hours.

members.name: m
members.summary: A duration of n minutes.

members.name: ms
members.summary: A duration of n milliseconds. The function form of a literal like 500ms.

members.name: parse
members.summary: Parse a duration in the form show prints, such as 1h30m, 2.5s or 500ms. Raises on anything else, including values finer than a millisecond.

members.name: s
members.summary: A duration of n seconds.

members.name: sleep
members.summary: Pause for the duration. Zero returns immediately; a negative duration raises. The OS timer resolution (about 15ms on Windows, 1ms on Linux) means a short sleep may last longer than asked, never shorter. It is called Duration.sleep so that plain `sleep` still runs the system command.

members.name: sum
members.summary: Sum durations.

members.name: toMillis
members.summary: The total milliseconds as an int, for example for ratios or JSON fields.

members.name: toSeconds
members.summary: The total seconds as a float, without losing precision (2500ms is 2.5).

members.name: tryParse
members.summary: Like Duration.parse, but returns None instead of raising.

members.name: fromFile
members.summary: Read `.env` lines (`KEY=value`) as EnvVar records.

members.name: get
members.summary: A process environment variable as an Option.

members.name: ofPairs
members.summary: Build EnvVar records from name/value tuples.

members.name: pair
members.summary: Build one EnvVar from a name and value.

members.name: vars
members.summary: Every environment variable as EnvVar records.

members.name: append
members.summary: Append a sequence of lines, safely even when other processes append to the same file. Each call is written as a single append (O_APPEND on Unix, append-only access on Windows), so its lines stay together and intact, and no lock blocks readers. If the system writes only part of the data (disk full, a size limit), the rest is retried and another writer's data may land in between. This holds on local filesystems, including bind mounts on the same host, but not on network filesystems (nfs, smb).

members.name: copy
members.summary: Copy a file from src to dst. The arguments are in the usual (src, dst) order rather than data-last, since neither one is the data. Raises, naming the path, if the destination exists; delete it first to overwrite.
members.example:
let d = Path.newTempDir ()
["x"] |> File.write $"{d}/a.txt"
File.copy $"{d}/a.txt" $"{d}/b.txt"
Dir.deleteAll d

members.name: delete
members.summary: Delete a file. Raises, naming the path, when it does not exist. Copy and move never overwrite, so delete the destination first when you want to replace it.
members.example:
let d = Path.newTempDir ()
["x"] |> File.write $"{d}/f.txt"
File.delete $"{d}/f.txt"
Dir.delete d

members.name: exists
members.summary: True when a path exists.

members.name: isExecutable
members.summary: True when the owner execute bit is set (the bit an installer sets). Simpler than checking File.mode with Str.contains "x". Follows symlinks like the other File.* queries; a missing path raises. Windows has no execute bit, so there the answer is based on the extension (.exe/.bat/.cmd/.com).

members.name: mode
members.summary: The path's permissions as text like rwxr-xr-x, wrapped in Some; None on Windows, which has no POSIX permissions. Like the other File.* queries it follows symlinks, so a broken link raises, naming the link. A typical use is checking for 0600 before File.readSecret: File.mode p == Some "rw-------".

members.name: move
members.summary: Move (rename) a file from src to dst. Raises if the destination exists.
members.example:
let d = Path.newTempDir ()
["x"] |> File.write $"{d}/a.txt"
File.move $"{d}/a.txt" $"{d}/b.txt"
Dir.deleteAll d

members.name: read
members.summary: Read a file's lines. The whole file is read immediately.

members.name: readBytes
members.summary: Read a file's raw bytes, exactly as stored, without decoding or splitting into lines (File.read does both and replaces invalid characters). The whole file is loaded into memory, so it is not meant for very large files.

members.name: readSecret
members.summary: Read a file's whole content as a Secret, for example a secret mounted into a container. Trailing newlines are removed.

members.name: sha256
members.summary: The SHA-256 digest of a file's bytes, as lowercase hex (same output as sha256sum). The file is streamed, never loaded into memory whole.

members.name: size
members.summary: The file's size as a Size, which you can compare directly (`File.size p > 10MiB`); use Size.toBytes to get an int. Raises when the file does not exist (there is no trySize yet).
members.example:
let d = Path.newTempDir ()
let f = $"{d}/a.txt"
["x"] |> File.write f
print $"{File.size f}"
Dir.deleteAll d

members.name: stat
members.summary: The FileRow for one path, the same row ls shows, so `Path.glob ... |> Seq.map File.stat` turns paths into rows. For a symlink it describes the link itself (kind Symlink, target Some), not what it points to. Raises when the path does not exist; note that a file found by glob may be deleted before stat reads it.
members.example:
let d = Path.newTempDir ()
let f = $"{d}/a.txt"
["x"] |> File.write f
print (File.stat f).name
Dir.deleteAll d

members.name: write
members.summary: Write a sequence of lines to a file, replacing its contents.

members.name: writeAtomic
members.summary: Write a sequence of lines by replacing the whole file at once: the content goes to a temp file in the same directory, is flushed to disk, and is then renamed over the target. Readers see either the complete old file or the complete new one, and a failed write leaves the original intact. For a symlink, the file it points to is replaced, not the link; the file's permissions and any existing BOM are kept. Because the file is a new inode, hard links are separated, open handles and tail -f keep seeing the old file, and a single-file bind mount into a container stops updating; use File.write when you need an in-place write. Inside a plan it records the same WriteFile op as File.write, and apply then does an in-place write.

members.name: writeBytes
members.summary: Write raw bytes to a file exactly as given (File.write instead encodes lines and ends each with LF).

members.name: abs
members.summary: The absolute value.

members.name: average
members.summary: The mean of a float sequence. Raises on an empty sequence or a non-finite result.

members.name: near
members.summary: True when a and b differ by at most eps. This is how to compare floats, since `==` does not accept them.

members.name: ofInt
members.summary: Convert an int to a float. weir never converts between them automatically.

members.name: parse
members.summary: Parse a float in the form show prints. Raises on anything else, including NaN and Infinity, because weir floats are always finite.

members.name: round
members.summary: Round to the nearest whole number, with halves rounded away from zero (2.5 becomes 3.0).

members.name: sum
members.summary: Add up a sequence of floats; raises if the sum is not finite. Seq.sum is for ints only; each numeric type has its own sum.

members.name: toInt
members.summary: The integer part, rounding toward zero. Raises when the value is outside the 64-bit int range.

members.name: tryParse
members.summary: Like Float.parse, but returns None instead of raising.

members.name: fold
members.summary: Fold over a graph that is discovered as you go. Nodes are taken from a first-in, first-out queue; a node whose key was already seen is skipped. The step returns the new accumulator and the node's children, which are added to the queue. It ends when the queue is empty. Cycles are safe, and after 100000 steps it raises instead of running forever. A node with key "" is never skipped as a duplicate.
members.example: [1] |> Frontier.fold (fun n -> show n) 0 (fun acc n -> (acc + n, if n < 3 then [n + 1] else []))

members.name: reach
members.summary: Every node reachable from a start node, breadth-first, each listed once; nodes with the same key count as one, so cycles are safe. The neighbors function defines the graph, so nothing has to be built up front.
members.example: Graph.reach (fun n -> show n) (fun n -> if n < 3 then [n + 1] else []) 1

members.name: defaults
members.summary: The default request: method = Get, empty url, NoAuth, no body, 30s timeout. Start from it with `Http.send { Http.defaults with url = u }`. `Http.get url` and the other method helpers return a request built from it.

members.name: delete
members.summary: Build a Delete request for the url.

members.name: expect
members.summary: Send a request and return the response body as lines. Raises on a non-2xx status; the error names the method, url and status and includes the start of the body. Use `Http.get url |> Http.expect` for a simple read; requests built with `with` work the same way. If you need to inspect an error response, use Http.send instead.

members.name: get
members.summary: Build a GET request for the url; nothing is sent yet. `Http.get u` is the same as `{ Http.defaults with method = Get; url = u }`. Send it with Http.send (returns the response, whatever the status) or Http.expect (returns the body, raises on failure). Set other fields with `with`: `Http.send { Http.get u with auth = Bearer t }`.

members.name: head
members.summary: Build a Head request for the url.

members.name: header
members.summary: The first value of a response header, or None when it is missing. Header names match case-insensitively, as HTTP requires, so ETag and etag are the same header. For headers that can repeat (Set-Cookie), use Http.headerAll.

members.name: headerAll
members.summary: Every value of a response header, in the order received, matching the name case-insensitively. Use it for headers that can repeat (Set-Cookie). Empty when the header is missing.

members.name: options
members.summary: Build an Options request for the url.

members.name: patch
members.summary: Build a Patch request for the url.

members.name: post
members.summary: Build a Post request for the url; add a body or auth with `with`.

members.name: put
members.summary: Build a Put request for the url.

members.name: query
members.summary: Build a QUERY request (RFC 10008) for the url. QUERY is idempotent by definition, so wrapping it in `retry` is safe. Few servers support it yet, so expect 405.

members.name: send
members.summary: Send a request and return the response. A non-2xx status such as 404 is returned, not raised; only network failures raise. A Json body sends `to json` output exactly as given. Auth values hold Secrets, and show masks them.

members.name: withQuery
members.summary: Add a query string to a url. The parameters come first and the url last, so it fits a pipe: `url |> Http.withQuery [(k, v)]`. Keys and values are percent-encoded, so a space or `&` cannot break the url. (Not to be confused with `Http.query`, which builds a QUERY request.)

members.name: epochMs
members.summary: Milliseconds since the Unix epoch, as an int. Useful for JSON fields and other tools (like `date +%s%3N`).

members.name: now
members.summary: The current instant (UTC).

members.name: ofEpochMs
members.summary: The instant for a number of milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

members.name: parse
members.summary: Parse an ISO 8601 timestamp with Z or a numeric offset, converted to UTC. A bare date means midnight UTC. Raises on anything else; use tryParse to get an Option instead.

members.name: parseWith
members.summary: Parse a timestamp using a format string: %Y %m %d %e (1-2 digit day) %b (Jan..Dec) %H %M %S %f %z, with %% for a literal %; any other text must match exactly. Only the start of the text has to match, so trailing text such as the rest of a log line is ignored. Without %z the time is UTC. Raises on a mismatch, naming the position.

members.name: tryParse
members.summary: Some instant, or None when the text is not ISO 8601.

members.name: tryParseWith
members.summary: Some instant, or None when the text does not match. An unknown directive in the format still raises, because that is a bug in the format, not in the data.

members.name: inferShape
members.summary: Generate draft `type` declarations from a JSON sample and return them as text; this is what `#infer` uses. The top record is named Root; nested records are named after their field, with array element types in the singular. Array elements are merged, and a key missing from some elements becomes an Option. An object used as a dictionary (values of one shape with mostly non-identifier keys, different keys in sibling objects, or an empty {}) becomes seq<string * _>. Notes are added as `//` lines. The draft only covers what the sample contains, so review and edit it. This runs on a sample at runtime; it does not affect type checking.
members.pointer: Like `weir add schema`, this turns outside data into a type declaration you paste into your script and own; it does not change how `check` or `from json` behave.

members.name: debug
members.summary: Write a DEBUG line to stderr; hidden unless WEIR_LOG=debug (or trace). All Log functions write to stderr so stdout stays free for data; there is no option to log to stdout.

members.name: debugWith
members.summary: Like Log.debug, but takes a function that builds the message, called only when debug logging is on.

members.name: info
members.summary: Write an INFO line to stderr. Shown by default; set WEIR_LOG to a level (case-insensitive) to change what is shown, or to off to silence logging.

members.name: infoWith
members.summary: Like Log.info, but takes a function that builds the message, called only when info logging is on.

members.name: trace
members.summary: Write a TRACE line to stderr. This is the most detailed level, hidden unless WEIR_LOG=trace.

members.name: traceWith
members.summary: Like Log.trace, but takes a function that builds the message, called only when trace logging is on. Plain Log.trace always builds its message, so use this when that is expensive.

members.name: warn
members.summary: Write a WARN line to stderr. This is the highest level, shown unless WEIR_LOG=off.

members.name: warnWith
members.summary: Like Log.warn, but takes a function that builds the message, called only when warnings are shown.

members.name: add
members.summary: A new map with the entry added, replacing any existing value for the key; the original is unchanged.

members.name: count
members.summary: The number of entries.

members.name: get
members.summary: The value for a key. Raises, naming the key, when it is missing; use tryGet to get an Option instead.

members.name: has
members.summary: True when a key is present.

members.name: keys
members.summary: The keys, sorted.

members.name: ofPairs
members.summary: Build a map from (key, value) pairs. If a key repeats, the last value wins, as when reading JSON.

members.name: pairs
members.summary: The entries as (key, value) pairs, key-sorted.

members.name: remove
members.summary: A new map without the key (a missing key is not an error); the original is unchanged.

members.name: tryGet
members.summary: Some value when the key is present, None when not.

members.name: values
members.summary: The values, in key-sorted order.

members.name: portOpen
members.summary: True when 127.0.0.1:<port> accepts a TCP connection within 250ms. Meant as a readiness check inside poll. Only local ports are supported for now.

members.name: bind
members.summary: Apply a function that itself returns an Option to the value inside Some, without nesting the result. Use it to chain lookups that may each fail.

members.name: defaultValue
members.summary: The Some value, or a fallback when None.

members.name: defaultWith
members.summary: Like defaultValue, but the fallback is computed only when None.

members.name: flatten
members.summary: Collapse a nested Option<Option<T>> into Option<T> (Some (Some x) -> Some x; any None -> None).

members.name: iter
members.summary: Run a side effect on the value inside Some; do nothing for None. Saves writing a match.

members.name: map
members.summary: Apply a function to the value inside Some; None stays None.

members.name: orElse
members.summary: The option itself when it is Some, otherwise the fallback option. The fallback comes first so it works in a pipe. The result is still an Option; use Option.defaultValue to unwrap. The fallback is evaluated even when the option is Some.

members.name: orElseWith
members.summary: Like orElse, but the fallback is a function (unit -> Option) called only when the option is None. Use it when the fallback is expensive to compute.

members.name: cacheHome
members.summary: The base directory for user cache: `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` (or `~/.cache`) on POSIX, `%LOCALAPPDATA%` on Windows.

members.name: combine
members.summary: Join two path segments.

members.name: configHome
members.summary: The base directory for user config: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (or `~/.config`) on POSIX, `%APPDATA%` on Windows.

members.name: dir
members.summary: The directory part of a path.

members.name: extension
members.summary: The extension, including the dot.

members.name: fileName
members.summary: The final component of a path.

members.name: glob
members.summary: The paths matching a glob pattern, lazily. `**` does not follow symlinks.

members.name: home
members.summary: The user's home directory, in the platform's native form and without a trailing separator. Has no side effects. In a command line, a typed `~` means this path; in an expression, build paths with `$"{Path.home ()}/.bashrc"`.

members.name: newTempDir
members.summary: Create a new, uniquely named directory under the temp root and return its path (named the same way as `within tmp`). It is never removed automatically; deleting it is up to you or the OS. For a directory that is removed when a block exits (also on Ctrl+C or kill), use `within tmp dir`.

members.name: normalize
members.summary: Resolve '.' and '..' segments in the text of a path, without touching the filesystem, using the current directory, or following symlinks. combine leaves '..' in place and under rejects paths that leave the base; use normalize when going up out of a directory is intended. A relative path keeps its leading '..' segments; at the root of an absolute path, '..' is dropped.

members.name: stateHome
members.summary: The base directory for user state: `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (or `~/.local/state`) on POSIX, `%LOCALAPPDATA%` on Windows. Where the REPL keeps its history.

members.name: stem
members.summary: The file name without its extension.

members.name: tempRoot
members.summary: The system temp directory, in the platform's native form and without a trailing separator. Has no side effects.

members.name: under
members.summary: Join a name onto base, normalize, and raise if the result ends up outside base. The check is by whole path segments, so uploads-evil is not inside uploads. Use combine for paths you control and under for paths you do not (such as user input). It works on the text only and never touches the disk or follows symlinks. An absolute or Windows-style name is rejected on every platform.

members.name: apply
members.summary: Carry out a plan's operations in the order they were recorded, using the normal functions. Stops at the first operation that fails; earlier ones stay done, since there is no rollback. Not allowed inside a `plan` block.

members.name: isEmpty
members.summary: True when the plan recorded no operations, for example because the script only read things.

members.name: ops
members.summary: The operations recorded in a plan, in the order they were recorded, as a seq<Op>. Useful for tests and inspection (`plan <block> == [WriteFile(p, c)]`); Op values can be compared and shown, with Secrets masked.

members.name: preview
members.summary: A readable description of a plan's operations, one line each. Nothing has been changed yet; only Plan.apply makes the changes. Secrets are masked.

members.name: defaults
members.summary: The default poll options: timeout = 1m, interval = 1s.

members.name: pid
members.summary: The child's OS process id.
members.pointer: within proc p = <command> binds the handle; see #help within

members.name: running
members.summary: True while the child has not exited.
members.pointer: `poll watch=p` checks this for you and gives better errors.

members.name: stop
members.summary: Kill the process and its children now and wait for them. Safe to call more than once; the block's exit then has nothing left to do.

members.name: tail
members.summary: The child's last ~100 lines of output (stderr first). You can read it while the process is still running.
members.pointer: Errors from `poll watch=…` include this automatically.

members.name: wait
members.summary: Wait until the child exits on its own and return its exit code. Use this to let a scoped process finish; otherwise it is killed when the block exits.

members.name: defaultValue
members.summary: The value inside Ok, or the fallback for an Error.

members.name: isOk
members.summary: True for Ok, false for an Error.

members.name: map
members.summary: Apply a function to the value inside Ok; an Error stays as it is.
members.example: File.read "n.txt" |> Seq.length |> try result |> Result.map (fun n -> n * 2)

members.name: toOption
members.summary: Some value for Ok, None for an Error (the message is dropped).

members.name: defaults
members.summary: The default retry options: attempts = 5, delay = 1s, timeout = None. `retry attempts=5` is short for `retry { Retry.defaults with attempts = 5 }`.

members.name: map
members.summary: Transform a secret's value while keeping it secret. `Secret.map (fun t -> "Bearer " + t)` gives a Secret, whereas revealing and then concatenating would give a plain string.

members.name: of
members.summary: Mark a computed string (a generated token, a derived key) as secret. show prints it as ***; only Secret.reveal gives back the plain value.

members.name: reveal
members.summary: The secret's plain value. This is the only way to get it out of a Secret, so each use (a header, a hash) is explicit and easy to find when auditing.

members.name: args
members.summary: The command-line arguments of the script that was run. The same in every module.

members.name: entryPath
members.summary: The path of the script that was run. Unlike scriptPath, it is the same in every module.

members.name: pid
members.summary: This process's id.

members.name: prompt
members.summary: Write a message to stderr and read one line from stdin, for interactive input. The prompt goes to stderr, so piped stdout still carries only data. Raises at end of input instead of returning an empty answer. To read the rest of stdin as a stream, use Self.stdin — both read the same input, so a line a prompt took is not seen again.
members.pointer: `let name = Self.prompt "your name?"`. In tests, pipe the answer in.

members.name: scriptPath
members.summary: The path of the file that contains this code; in a module, the module's own path.

members.name: stdin
members.summary: This process's standard input, as lazy lines. The same in every module.

members.name: append
members.summary: Concatenate two sequences, lazily.

members.name: average
members.summary: The mean of an int sequence, as a float. Raises on an empty sequence. For floats, sizes and durations use Float.average, Size.average or Duration.average.

members.name: choose
members.summary: Apply a function that returns an Option and keep only the Some values, lazily.
members.example: [1; 2; 3] |> Seq.choose (fun x -> if x > 1 then Some x else None) |> Seq.freeze

members.name: chunkBySize
members.summary: Split into consecutive batches of at most n elements, lazily. The last batch may be shorter.

members.name: collect
members.summary: Map each element to a sequence and flatten the results into one, lazily (flatMap in other languages).

members.name: concat
members.summary: Flatten a sequence of sequences into one, lazily.

members.name: contains
members.summary: True when an element is present.

members.name: countBy
members.summary: Count the elements per key as (key, count) pairs, in the order each key is first seen. The whole input is read when the first pair is requested.

members.name: distinct
members.summary: Drop duplicate elements, keeping first order.

members.name: distinctBy
members.summary: Keep only the first element for each key, lazily. Like distinct, but compares by a key function.

members.name: equal
members.summary: True when both sequences have the same length and equal elements in order. Elements must support equality, as for Seq.contains. It stops at the first mismatch without reading further. Prefer it to joining and comparing strings, which can give a wrong answer when elements contain the separator.

members.name: exactlyOne
members.summary: The only element. Raises if there are none or more than one (unlike head, which quietly ignores extra elements). Use it for command output that should be exactly one line.

members.name: except
members.summary: The elements of the sequence that are not in the excluded values. The excluded values come first and are read in full on the first request; the sequence itself is read lazily.

members.name: exists
members.summary: True when any element satisfies a predicate.

members.name: find
members.summary: The first element a predicate accepts. Raises when none match; use tryFind to get an Option instead.

members.name: fold
members.summary: Combine the elements from left to right, starting from an initial accumulator.

members.name: forall
members.summary: True when every element satisfies a predicate.

members.name: freeze
members.summary: Evaluate a lazy sequence now and keep the results.
members.pointer: Freeze a sequence you will read more than once, or to capture its contents now (such as a command's output or a directory listing) before something changes them.

members.name: groupBy
members.summary: Group elements by a key into (key, items) pairs, as in F#.

members.name: head
members.summary: The first element (raises on empty).

members.name: indexed
members.summary: Pair every element with its zero-based index, lazily. For F#'s mapi/iteri, use `indexed |> map`/`iter` on the pairs.

members.name: isEmpty
members.summary: True when the sequence has no elements.

members.name: item
members.summary: The element at a zero-based index (raises out of range).

members.name: iter
members.summary: Run a unit-returning effect over each element.

members.name: last
members.summary: The last element. Raises 'last: empty sequence' when empty; Seq.tryLast returns None instead. It reads the whole sequence, so it never returns on an infinite one.

members.name: length
members.summary: Count the elements (forces the sequence).

members.name: map
members.summary: Apply a function to every element, lazily.

members.name: max
members.summary: The largest element, found in one pass without sorting. Elements must be comparable; raises on an empty sequence.

members.name: maxBy
members.summary: The element with the largest key. Keys must be comparable; raises on an empty sequence.

members.name: min
members.summary: The smallest element, found in one pass without sorting. Elements must be comparable; raises on an empty sequence.

members.name: minBy
members.summary: The element with the smallest key. Keys must be comparable; raises on an empty sequence.

members.name: pairwise
members.summary: Adjacent pairs: (e0,e1), (e1,e2), and so on.

members.name: pfirst
members.summary: Run the function on every element in parallel and return the first successful result. Processes started by the others are killed, along with their children. If every call fails, the error of the earliest element is raised; an empty sequence raises. Errors from the calls that did not win are discarded, so if only one element can ever succeed, the others' errors stay hidden and a misconfiguration can go unnoticed.
members.pointer: A race, not a retry: for example the same download from several mirrors, where the first answer wins and the losers' processes are killed.

members.name: pfirstWith
members.summary: Seq.pfirst with a maximum number of parallel calls.

members.name: pick
members.summary: Apply a function to each element and return the value of the first Some result. Raises when there is none; use tryPick to get an Option instead.

members.name: piter
members.summary: Run an effect over each element in parallel.
members.pointer: Each worker gets its own copy of the session: a `cd` inside a worker affects only that worker and is gone when the workers finish.

members.name: piterWith
members.summary: Seq.piter with an explicit worker count.
members.pointer: Plain `piter` uses fewer workers when parallel calls are nested; the n you give here is always used as is.

members.name: pmap
members.summary: Map in parallel across worker threads.
members.pointer: Results keep the input order. It runs eagerly with up to 64 workers; if several items fail, the error from the earliest item is the one reported.

members.name: pmapWith
members.summary: Seq.pmap with an explicit number of workers. Use it when the work is rate-limited or uses a lot of memory.
members.pointer: Plain `pmap` uses fewer workers when parallel calls are nested; the n you give here is always used as is.

members.name: range
members.summary: A lazy arithmetic range: start, step, stop.

members.name: reduce
members.summary: Like fold without an initial value: the first element is the starting accumulator. Raises on an empty sequence; use fold when you have a starting value.

members.name: replicate
members.summary: A sequence of n copies of a value, lazily. Raises on a negative count.

members.name: rev
members.summary: Reverse the sequence. The whole input is read when the first element is requested, so it cannot be used on an infinite sequence.

members.name: scan
members.summary: Like fold, but returns every intermediate accumulator, starting with the initial value, lazily.

members.name: skip
members.summary: Drop the first n elements, keep the rest lazily.

members.name: skipWhile
members.summary: Drop leading elements while the predicate holds, then return all the rest, lazily.

members.name: sort
members.summary: Sort the elements in ascending order (they must be comparable). The whole input is read when the first element is requested.

members.name: sortBy
members.summary: Order by a key projection.

members.name: sortByDescending
members.summary: Order by a key projection, descending.

members.name: sortDescending
members.summary: Sort the elements in descending order (they must be comparable). The whole input is read when the first element is requested.

members.name: sum
members.summary: Add the elements of an int sequence.

members.name: take
members.summary: The first n elements, lazily; pairs with Seq.skip.

members.name: takeWhile
members.summary: The leading elements for which the predicate holds, lazily; stops at the first one that fails.

members.name: tryExactlyOne
members.summary: Like exactlyOne, but returns an Option: Some when there is exactly one element, None otherwise.

members.name: tryFind
members.summary: The first element a predicate accepts, as an Option.

members.name: tryHead
members.summary: The first element as an Option, None when empty.

members.name: tryItem
members.summary: The element at an index as an Option.

members.name: tryLast
members.summary: The last element as an Option, None when empty. Reads the whole sequence.

members.name: tryPick
members.summary: Apply a function to each element and return the first Some result, or None.

members.name: tryReduce
members.summary: Like reduce, but returns an Option: Some result, or None for an empty sequence (where reduce raises).

members.name: where
members.summary: Keep the elements a predicate accepts, lazily.

members.name: windowed
members.summary: Sliding windows of n consecutive elements, produced lazily. A source shorter than n gives an empty sequence (there are no partial windows). The windows share the same cached elements. Raises when n <= 0.

members.name: zip
members.summary: Pair two sequences element-wise, stopping at the shorter.

members.name: port
members.summary: The port the listener bound.
members.pointer: within serve srv = { port = 8080; maxConcurrent = 4 } handler binds the handle; see #help within

members.name: running
members.summary: True while the listener is still open (the scope has not exited).

members.name: streamErrors
members.summary: Error messages from Stream response bodies that raised partway through; the client received a truncated body for each. Empty until one fails. Streaming errors are reported here instead of being raised out of the handler.
members.pointer: When a Stream body raises, the client's response is cut off and the error is recorded here.

members.name: average
members.summary: The mean size, truncated to whole bytes. Raises on an empty sequence.

members.name: bytes
members.summary: A size of n bytes. The function form of a literal like 512B.

members.name: parse
members.summary: Parse a size. Binary units are powers of 1024 (1.5MiB); SI units are powers of 10 (1MB is 10^6 bytes); B means bytes. Raises if the value is not a whole number of bytes.

members.name: sum
members.summary: Add up sizes; the total is a Size.

members.name: toBytes
members.summary: The exact number of bytes as an int. (show truncates sizes to one decimal place.)

members.name: tryParse
members.summary: Like Size.parse, but returns None instead of raising.

members.name: contains
members.summary: True when a substring is present.

members.name: endsWith
members.summary: True when the string ends with a suffix.

members.name: fields
members.summary: Split on runs of whitespace (the same whitespace trim removes) into fields. Never produces empty pieces; a blank or empty string gives an empty sequence.

members.name: fromBase64
members.summary: Decode standard base64 (padded or unpadded) to text. Raises on invalid base64 or when the decoded bytes are not valid UTF-8, instead of silently inserting replacement characters.

members.name: fromUtf8
members.summary: Decode Bytes as UTF-8 text. Raises when the bytes are not valid UTF-8 or contain a NUL byte, so corrupt data is never decoded silently.

members.name: isMatch
members.summary: True when a regex matches anywhere in the string.

members.name: join
members.summary: Join a sequence of strings with a separator.

members.name: length
members.summary: The number of characters.

members.name: padLeft
members.summary: Pad with spaces on the left to a total width, for right-aligned columns. A string already that long is unchanged; a negative width raises.

members.name: padRight
members.summary: Pad with spaces on the right to a total width, for left-aligned columns (like printf "%-15s"). A string already that long is unchanged; a negative width raises.

members.name: replace
members.summary: Replace every occurrence of a substring.

members.name: replicate
members.summary: The string repeated n times. 0 gives the empty string; a negative count raises, as in Seq.replicate.

members.name: rmatch
members.summary: The groups of the first regex match as Some sequence, or None when there is no match. Groups are positional: named groups `(?<x>...)` are rejected, because in weir you name captures when you bind them.

members.name: rmatchAll
members.summary: Every regex match's groups, as a sequence of sequences.

members.name: rsplit
members.summary: Split on every regex match. As with split, empty pieces are kept (adjacent matches, or a match at either end, produce ""). Capture groups do not add extra pieces.

members.name: rsplitOnce
members.summary: Split at the last occurrence of the separator into (before, after). Raises when the separator is missing; tryRsplitOnce returns an Option instead. Useful for host:port when the host may contain colons.

members.name: sha256
members.summary: The SHA-256 digest of the string's UTF-8 bytes, as lowercase hex (same output as sha256sum). Only SHA-256 is available for now.

members.name: split
members.summary: Split on a separator into a sequence. Empty pieces are kept: adjacent separators, or a separator at either end, produce "".

members.name: splitOnce
members.summary: Split at the first occurrence of the separator into (before, after); the after part is kept whole, including any later separators. Raises when the separator is missing; trySplitOnce returns an Option instead.

members.name: startsWith
members.summary: True when the string starts with a prefix.

members.name: sub
members.summary: A substring by start index and length.

members.name: toBase64
members.summary: Base64 of the string's UTF-8 bytes, on one line. It is never wrapped at 76 columns, so there is no need for base64 -w0.

members.name: toInt
members.summary: Parse an int (raises on a non-number).

members.name: toLower
members.summary: Lowercase (invariant culture).

members.name: toUpper
members.summary: Uppercase (invariant culture).

members.name: toUtf8
members.summary: The string's UTF-8 bytes as a Bytes value.

members.name: trim
members.summary: Drop leading and trailing whitespace.

members.name: trimEnd
members.summary: Drop trailing whitespace.

members.name: trimStart
members.summary: Drop leading whitespace.

members.name: tryFromBase64
members.summary: Like fromBase64, but returns an Option: None both for malformed base64 and for valid base64 that does not decode to text.

members.name: tryFromUtf8
members.summary: Like fromUtf8, but returns an Option: None when the bytes are not text (including bytes with NUL).

members.name: tryIndexOf
members.summary: The index of a substring as an Option.

members.name: tryRsplitOnce
members.summary: Like rsplitOnce, but returns an Option: Some (before, after) at the last occurrence, None when the separator is missing.
members.example: match Str.tryRsplitOnce "@" "a@b@host" with | Some (u, h) -> print h | None -> print "no"

members.name: trySplitOnce
members.summary: Like splitOnce, but returns an Option: Some (before, after) at the first occurrence, None when the separator is missing. Handy for parsing `KEY=VALUE`.
members.example: match Str.trySplitOnce "=" "key=val" with | Some (k, v) -> print k | None -> print "no"

members.name: tryToInt
members.summary: Parse an int as an Option, None when it is not a number.

members.name: inferShape
members.summary: Generate a draft row `type` declaration from a sample of column-aligned output and return it as text; this is what `#infer … from table` uses. Each column's type comes from its values: int if all are ints, otherwise float or bool if they all fit, otherwise string; a column with empty or `<none>` cells becomes an Option, with a note. Headers become field names, with `[<Wire>]` added when the original header cannot be recovered from the name. A note says the result is read as seq<Root>. Review and edit the draft. This runs on a sample at runtime; it does not affect type checking.
members.pointer: Like `weir add schema`, this turns outside data into a type declaration you paste into your script and own; it does not change how `check` or `from table` behave.

members.name: render
members.summary: Format a seq of records of the same type as aligned table lines for `print`, with a bold header and the same layout the REPL uses. It is for display only: there is no `to table`, and a table cannot be read back reliably, so use `to json` or `to yaml` to exchange data. The table is fitted to the terminal width, and not limited when piped. A seq of non-records is an error that points at the location.

members.name: width
members.summary: The terminal width in columns, read each time it is called, so resizes are picked up. Returns 80 instead of raising when there is no terminal (output piped or redirected). Use it to size output, like `tput cols`.

members.name: walk
members.summary: Walk a tree for its side effects, parents before children. The step function does the work for a node and returns its children, so which children exist can depend on what the parent did. Nodes are not de-duplicated; for structures with cycles use Graph.reach or Frontier.fold. The 100000-step limit still applies.
members.example: 1 |> Tree.walk (fun n -> if n < 3 then [n + 1] else [])

members.name: fromBytes
members.summary: The uuid of 16 big-endian bytes. Raises on any other length.

members.name: instant
members.summary: Some creation instant for a version 7 uuid (millisecond precision); None for every other version.

members.name: max
members.summary: The all-ones uuid. It sorts after every other uuid.

members.name: nil
members.summary: The all-zero uuid, used to mean "no uuid".

members.name: ns
members.summary: The RFC 9562 namespaces for v5: `dns`, `url`, `oid`, `x500`. Any uuid works as a namespace of your own.

members.name: parse
members.summary: Parse a uuid: 8-4-4-4-12 hex digits or 32 digits without dashes, in any case, with an optional urn:uuid: prefix. Every version and variant is accepted. Raises on anything else; use tryParse to get an Option instead.

members.name: toBytes
members.summary: The 16 bytes in big-endian (network) order, the same order as the text form.

members.name: toString
members.summary: The standard text form: lowercase 8-4-4-4-12. This is what show, JSON and command arguments use.

members.name: tryParse
members.summary: Some uuid, or None when the text is not one (including braces and other platform-specific forms).

members.name: v4
members.summary: A random uuid (version 4), from the system's cryptographic generator.

members.name: v5
members.summary: The name-based uuid (version 5): SHA-1 over the namespace's bytes and the name's UTF-8 bytes. The same name in the same namespace always gives the same uuid.

members.name: v7
members.summary: A time-ordered uuid (version 7): epoch milliseconds, then a counter and random bits. Values are strictly increasing within this process, so they sort by creation time both as uuids and as text.

members.name: v7At
members.summary: A version 7 uuid for the given instant, truncated to milliseconds. Use it for records that carry their own timestamp. If the instant is between the last generated uuid and now, it sorts correctly with v7 uuids; an earlier or future instant gets random bits and no ordering guarantee. Raises for instants before the Unix epoch.

members.name: version
members.summary: The version field: 4, 5, 7 and so on (0 for nil, 15 for max). Meaningful for the RFC 9562 variant.

members.name: inferShape
members.summary: Generate draft `type` declarations from a YAML sample and return them as text; this is what `#infer` uses. The top record is named Root and nested records are named automatically. Array elements are merged, and a key missing from some elements becomes an Option. An object used as a dictionary (values of one shape with mostly non-identifier keys, different keys in sibling objects, or an empty {}) becomes seq<string * _>. Notes are added as `//` lines. The draft only covers what the sample contains, so review and edit it. This runs on a sample at runtime; it does not affect type checking.
members.example:
let sample = <<<
    name: web
    port: 8080
print (Yaml.inferShape sample)
members.pointer: Like `weir add schema`, this turns outside data into a type declaration you paste into your script and own; it does not change how `check` or `from yaml` behave.

members.name: merge
members.summary: Apply a `yaml patch` block to a document. The patch's structure says where each change goes: mappings are merged recursively; sequence items are appended if missing, or updated/removed by the key given with `by=<key>`; scalars are replaced; `$-` removes a key or a matching item. The order of entries does not matter and applying a patch twice changes nothing more. Write the result with `to yaml`.
members.pointer: Define the patch with `let p = yaml patch by=name` and indented patch lines, then run `File.read f |> Yaml.parse |> Yaml.merge p |> to yaml |> File.write f`.

members.name: parse
members.summary: Parse one YAML document (the same strict subset) into Yaml nodes without a declared type. Every key is kept, including ones `from yaml T` would drop. Scalar types follow the same rules as in a `yaml` block: unquoted true/3/1.5 become YBool/YInt/YFloat, quoted or block scalars become YStr, and empty values become YNull.

forms.name: Completed
forms.summary: A finished command: exitCode, stdout, stderr. You get one from `| complete`.

forms.name: EnvVar
forms.summary: A name/value environment pair. From `Env.vars` / `pair` / `ofPairs` / `fromFile`.

forms.name: FileRow
forms.summary: A directory entry, as returned by `ls`. Fields: name; kind (Regular, Directory or Symlink); target (Some link target for a symlink, None otherwise; no File.* function gives you this); bytes (0 B for a directory); modified (the last-write time as an Instant, which does not change after you read it; tables show it as relative time, show prints ISO); hidden; and path. `ls` lists files and subdirectories sorted by name, case-sensitively with uppercase first, regardless of locale. Use name for matching and display and path when calling File.* functions. Less common details are separate functions rather than fields, such as File.mode for permissions.

forms.name: cd
forms.summary: Change the session's directory and return the previous one, so you can go back later (`let prev = cd "/tmp"`). A bare name uses the value of that binding (`cd target`). `cd` with no argument, or a typed `cd ~`, goes to the home directory; a string argument is used literally. To change directory for a block only, use `within cd`.

forms.name: complete
forms.summary: Run the command (or pipeline) and capture everything as a `Completed` record: its exit code, stdout and stderr. A nonzero exit does not raise.
forms.pointer: Use it when you need the exit code and the output together: `let r = git push | complete`, then read `r.exitCode`, `r.stdout`, `r.stderr`.

forms.name: exec
forms.summary: Replace weir's process with the command (execve), so it never returns. The program keeps weir's process id, which means a container entrypoint receives signals directly. It cannot take piped stdin.
forms.pointer: Like `fail` and `exit`, it ends the script, so it fits in any branch, whatever type the other branches have.

forms.name: exit
forms.summary: Exit the process with a status code.

forms.name: exitCode
forms.summary: Run the command with its output streaming to the terminal and return its exit code as an int. It never raises.
forms.pointer: Bind or match the result, as in `let rc = make test | exitCode`. Using it as a bare statement is an error, because the code would be thrown away.

forms.name: fail
forms.summary: Stop with a message and exit code 1.
forms.pointer: Use `exit n` to exit with a code and no message. fail never returns (its type is `string -> 'a`), so it can stand in any branch, for example opposite a branch that returns a value.

forms.name: freeze
forms.summary: Evaluate a lazy sequence now and keep the results. Same as Seq.freeze.

forms.name: from json
forms.summary: Parse one JSON document, which may span several lines (so a pretty-printed HTTP body can be piped straight in), into a declared record. Fields can be int, string, bool, float, or an Option of one of those; a missing key or null becomes None.
forms.pointer: Use it as a pipe stage: `resp.body |> from json Config`.

forms.name: from jsonl
forms.summary: Parse JSON lines (NDJSON, one document per line, as `to jsonl` writes) into declared records.
forms.pointer: Use it as a pipe stage: `xs |> from jsonl Config`.

forms.name: from table
forms.summary: Parse column-aligned tool output (a header row followed by aligned rows) into declared records, giving a seq<T>. Columns are cut at the header positions, not at every space, so a value with spaces (`Up 2 hours`) stays whole; headers are separated by 2 or more spaces (`CONTAINER ID` is one column). Fields match headers by their letters and digits, ignoring case (`podTemplateHash` matches `POD-TEMPLATE-HASH`); `[<Wire "HEADER">]` matches a header exactly. Cells are trimmed and converted to the field type (string, int, float, bool); for an Option field, an empty or `<none>` cell becomes None. Extra columns and blank lines are ignored, and errors report the line and column. Reading only; there is no `to table`.
forms.pointer: Use it as a pipe stage on a tool's table output: `… |> from table Pod`.

forms.name: from toml
forms.summary: Parse one TOML document (TOML 1.1, so every 1.0 file too) into a declared record, the same way `from yaml` does: nested records for tables, seqs for arrays and arrays of tables, Option for a key that may be missing, [<Wire "key">] for a key that is not a weir name (`current-context`, `requires-python`). Duplicate keys and redefined tables are errors, with the line. A date or time is read as its text; an offset date-time can be read into an Instant field with [<Iso8601>]. Reading only; there is no `to toml`.
forms.pointer: Use it as a pipe stage: `File.read "Cargo.toml" |> from toml Cargo`.

forms.name: from xml
forms.summary: Parse one XML document (a .csproj, .slnx or any XML) into a declared record. The root element is the record, and each field matches a child element by local name (a default xmlns is ignored). Use [<Attr>] to read an attribute, [<Elem "X">] for a repeated child, and a nested record for a child element. All values are text: fields are string, Option<string>, a record, or a seq of these, so declare a number as string and convert it with Str.toInt. Reading only; there is no `to xml`.
forms.pointer: Use it as a pipe stage: `File.read "App.csproj" |> from xml Proj`.

forms.name: from yaml
forms.summary: Parse YAML into declared records. Supports a strict subset: block mappings and sequences, scalars, # comments, and multiple documents separated by ---. Fields can be nested records, seqs, seq<string * _> for mappings, and Option (a missing key or null becomes None). Anchors, tags and flow style are rejected.
forms.pointer: Use it as a pipe stage: `lines |> from yaml Deployment` gives a seq<Deployment>, one per YAML document.

forms.name: let pure
forms.summary: Mark a binding as pure: `let pure f x = …` asserts that its whole body has no side effects, and `weir check` reports an error if it does. It works the same as wrapping the body in a `pure` block; hover shows the binding with a (pure) badge.
forms.pointer: See `#help pure` for the block form and the list of effects.

forms.name: line
forms.summary: Run a one-value command and return its single line of output as a trimmed string — for tools like `git rev-parse HEAD` or `az … -o tsv`. Raises on a nonzero exit, or when the output is not exactly one line.
forms.pointer: For several lines use `| text` (one string), or bind the command itself (a seq<string>, one element per line).

forms.name: not
forms.summary: Boolean negation.

forms.name: orFail
forms.summary: Run the command with its output streaming to the terminal; if it exits nonzero, raise with your message and the exit code.
forms.pointer: Use it to stop the script when a command fails: `make test | orFail "tests failed"`.

forms.name: poll
forms.summary: Like retry, but bounded by time instead of attempts: `poll timeout=5m interval=10s` followed by a body that checks readiness. With `watch=<proc>`, poll fails immediately if that scoped process dies (the error includes its last output), and a timeout error reports the process's state.
forms.pointer: To wait for a server to come up, start it with `within proc srv = …`, then `poll timeout=10s watch=srv` with `Net.portOpen <port>` as the body.

forms.name: print
forms.summary: Write a value and a trailing newline to stdout. Takes a string, int, float, bool, or seq<string> (one line per element); for anything else, render through an interpolation hole ($"{row}") or show.

forms.name: printerr
forms.summary: Write a value and a newline to stderr. Use it for diagnostics and keep stdout for data. Accepts the same types as print: string, int, float, bool, or seq<string>.

forms.name: pure
forms.summary: Assert that an indented block has no side effects: no filesystem, commands, network, environment, console or clock. If the block can reach one, `weir check` reports an error naming it. This is opt-in; code outside a pure block is not restricted.
forms.pointer: To mark a whole function, use `let pure`. Calls the checker cannot see into (a function parameter, a member of an import) count as impure, so the check may reject code that is actually pure, but it never accepts code that is not.

forms.name: retry
forms.summary: Re-run an indented body until it succeeds: `retry attempts=5 delay=30s` followed by the body. If the body returns a bool, true means success. If it returns another value, add `until r` and a predicate block; retry then returns the value that passed. Running out of attempts raises. An error raised inside the body is not retried, it propagates; to retry a failing command, turn its result into data with `| succeeds` or `| complete`.
forms.pointer: The options are a record, so you can also write `retry { Retry.defaults with attempts = 3 }`.

forms.name: show
forms.summary: Turn any value into its text form, the same text string interpolation produces. Use it where interpolation does not fit, such as `Seq.map show`. A Secret cannot be interpolated, but `show` renders it masked. It works on every value; functions show as an opaque placeholder.

forms.name: succeeds
forms.summary: Run the command and return true if it exited 0. Its output is discarded.
forms.pointer: Use it in a condition: `if git diff --quiet | succeeds then …`.

forms.name: text
forms.summary: Run the command and return its whole output as one string: lines joined with newlines, trailing blank lines dropped (like bash's `$(…)`). Raises on a nonzero exit.
forms.pointer: To keep the exit code instead of raising, use `| complete`.

forms.name: to json
forms.summary: Write one value as a single-line JSON document. A record becomes an object and a seq becomes an array (the whole seq is read first). A None field is left out, so from json reads it back as None.
forms.pointer: Use it as a pipe stage: `payload |> to json`.

forms.name: to jsonl
forms.summary: Write a sequence as JSON lines (NDJSON, one document per element, as `from jsonl` reads), lazily.
forms.pointer: Use it as a pipe stage: `xs |> to jsonl`.

forms.name: to yaml
forms.summary: Write one value as a YAML document. A record becomes a mapping, a seq a sequence, and a seq of pairs a mapping. `to yaml stream` writes one document per element, separated by `---`. A None field is left out; strings that YAML could misread as another type (no, 007, 1e5) are quoted.
forms.pointer: Use it as a pipe stage: `deployment |> to yaml`.

forms.name: try
forms.summary: Turn a failure into a value: `<expr> |> try` gives Some value, or None if evaluating the expression raised (a failed command, a parse error, a fail, a missing file). `<expr> |> try result` gives Ok value or Error message instead. Everything to the left of `|> try` is captured, and its value is fully evaluated inside, so a lazy sequence cannot fail later. `exit` still exits, and effects that happened before the failure are not undone.
forms.example: File.read "Cargo.toml" |> from toml {| package: {| version: string |} |} |> try
forms.pointer: Commands have their own form: `<command> | complete` gives the exit code and output as a record.

forms.name: within
forms.summary: Open a resource for an indented block. It is released however the block exits, normally or by an error. The kinds: `tmp` — a fresh directory, removed when the block exits; `cd` — the working directory for the block, restored after; `env` — environment variables set for the commands the block runs; `proc` — a background process, stopped together with anything it started when the block exits; `serve` — an HTTP server that runs until the block exits; its port is freed however the block ends; `lock` — an advisory file lock, held for the block and released however it ends, even on kill -9.
forms.pointer: `within proc srv = <command>` binds a Proc handle; the process and its children are killed and reaped when the block exits.
